newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy economy sluggish, exports, imports fall.
newsitem.headline: Italy economy sluggish, exports, imports fall.

text.p: The Italian economy ended 1996 on a low note, with industrial output in decline and exports and imports doing worse than expected, national statistics office Istat said Friday.
Italy's gross domestic product rose just 0.8 percent in 1996, compared with a jump of 3 percent the year before, according to provisional Istat figures, which were in line with official forecasts.
The country is striving to get its economy in shape for the 1999 launch of European economic and monetary union.

In the final three months of last year, the economy fell 0.1 percent against the third quarter -- the second time negative quarterly growth was registered during 1996. On the year-on-year level, GDP rose a meagre 0.5 percent.
An Istat spokesman said the dip in quarterly GDP was largely caused by a decline in industrial output, which was only partially offset by a slight improvement in the service sector.

The statistics office gave no further details, but figures released last week showed industrial production tumbling an unexpected 3.1 percent year-on-year in December. Full GDP data for 1996 will be presented to parliament next month.
